result.title: Spatial Memory for AR Glasses: Hierarchical Visual Acquisition and Source-Linked Recall
result.summary: We present a spatial-memory system that enables optical see-through AR glasses to recall earlier physical encounters. The dual-camera prototype combines hierarchical visual acquisition with source-linked storage and staged retrieval. Quality screen-ing, global and regional appearance novelty, and temporal support select monochrome observations for detailed RGB cap-ture. Semantic observations retain links to their source images, allowing retrieval to answer indexed historical questions direct-ly or inspect visual details omitted from scene descriptions. The architecture separates capture acceptance, interpretation out-come, and support for a particular question. This distinction motivates two core control mechanisms: bounded reassessment of familiar views when earlier processing leaves an evidence gap, and retention guided by source dependencies. In a 131.35 s egocentric replay, the implemented acquisition policy selected six RGB views from 648 monitoring observations, while feature extraction ran on 97.7% of observations. These results demon-strate selective RGB acquisition and identify frequent local inference as a remaining cost. Exposure duration and cross-view timing further constrain the evidence preserved from se-lected encounters. The system provides a practical acquisition-to-recall architecture for persistent AR assistance, with explicit boundaries between captured evidence, indexed interpretations, and supported historical claims.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向AR眼镜的空间记忆系统：双摄像头分级视觉采集、带源链接的存储与分阶段检索，使系统能直接回答历史视觉问题或回查被描述省略的原始图像细节；131秒自我中心回放中从648次监测观察里选出6帧RGB。
AI.relevance_reason: 其选择性RGB采集、证据缺口触发的有界重评估与源依赖保留，可能为长视觉流中的LOOK/STOP决策与证据可追溯性提供机制参照，但论文不涉及latent推理状态，需核查其成本结构与泛化。
